entries.title: Disable the AllJoyn Router service
entries.description: Sets the AllJoyn Router (AJRouter) service to Disabled and stops it. AllJoyn was an IoT device-interoperability transport.
entries.rationale: AllJoyn was retired and the service was removed in Windows 11 24H2; on earlier builds nothing on a normal desktop uses it. It is trigger-started, so this only ensures it can never start.
sideEffects: AllJoyn IoT device discovery and control (rare) stops working.
The service is removed entirely on Windows 11 24H2, where this is a harmless no-op.

entries.title: Disable the ActiveX Installer service
entries.description: Sets the ActiveX Installer (AxInstSV) service to Disabled and stops it. It handles installation of ActiveX controls for legacy Internet Explorer.
entries.rationale: ActiveX is an Internet Explorer feature that modern browsers do not use; Microsoft lists this service as safe to disable.
sideEffects: Legacy sites that install ActiveX controls through Internet Explorer or IE mode can no longer do so.

entries.title: Disable the Fax service
entries.description: Sets the Fax service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The Fax service is only used by the Windows Fax and Scan app and is not present on recent clean installs; disabling it reclaims a background service on machines with no fax modem.
sideEffects: Sending and receiving faxes through Windows Fax and Scan stops working.

entries.title: Disable the Windows Mobile Hotspot service
entries.description: Sets the Windows Mobile Hotspot (icssvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service backs the Mobile Hotspot feature and is trigger-started; disabling it prevents sharing this PC's connection over Wi-Fi for users who never use that feature.
sideEffects: The Mobile Hotspot feature (sharing this PC's internet connection over Wi-Fi) can no longer be turned on.

entries.title: Disable the Geolocation service
entries.description: Sets the Geolocation service (lfsvc) to Disabled and stops it, so Windows and apps can no longer determine this device's location.
entries.rationale: Removes the system-wide location provider (GPS, Wi-Fi and IP based). This is a privacy control; because it also breaks several convenience features it is a Strict-tier opt-in. The per-app location consent toggle is a lighter alternative.
sideEffects: Location stops working for all apps, Maps, weather-widget location and Find My Device.
Automatic time-zone (Set time zone automatically) can no longer update, because it depends on this service.
Wi-Fi-based location is unavailable.

entries.title: Disable the Downloaded Maps Manager service
entries.description: Sets the Downloaded Maps Manager (MapsBroker) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service only maintains offline maps for the deprecated Maps app; Microsoft lists it as safe to disable. It starts automatically (delayed), so disabling it removes one delayed-autostart service.
sideEffects: Offline maps in the (deprecated) Windows Maps app no longer download or update.

entries.title: Disable Network Connected Devices Auto-Setup
entries.description: Sets the Network Connected Devices Auto-Setup (NcdAutoSetup) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service automatically discovers and sets up networked devices such as printers and smart TVs it finds on the LAN; disabling it stops that automatic reach-out, a small privacy win. Devices can still be added manually.
sideEffects: Network devices (printers, media receivers, TVs) are no longer set up automatically when discovered; add them manually instead.

entries.title: Disable the Program Compatibility Assistant service
entries.description: Sets the Program Compatibility Assistant (PcaSvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: PCA shows 'this app might not have installed correctly' prompts, auto-applies compatibility modes and reports application-install data to Windows telemetry; Microsoft lists it as safe to disable. It starts automatically (delayed).
sideEffects: Compatibility-assistant prompts and automatic compatibility-mode application no longer appear.
Application-install signals are no longer sent to Windows telemetry.

entries.title: Disable the Phone Service
entries.description: Sets the Phone Service (PhoneSvc) to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service backs telephony state for Phone Link calling and some VoIP dialer integration. Disabling it is a Strict-tier opt-in for users who do not use PC calling.
sideEffects: Phone Link calling and VoIP apps that rely on the dialer integration (for example Teams calling) may stop working.

entries.title: Disable the Windows PushToInstall service
entries.description: Sets the Windows PushToInstall (PushToInstall) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service lets the Microsoft Store push a remote install to this device from a web page ('install to my devices'); disabling it removes that remote-install channel.
sideEffects: Installing a Store app remotely from microsoft.com to this device no longer works; install from the Store on the device instead.

entries.title: Keep the Remote Registry service disabled
entries.description: Ensures the Remote Registry (RemoteRegistry) service is set to Disabled and stopped, so the registry cannot be edited from another computer over the network.
entries.rationale: Remote Registry lets remote users modify this machine's registry and is a well-known attack surface. It ships Disabled; this control re-asserts that state if something enabled it.
sideEffects: Remote registry administration of this PC from another computer is not possible (it is not by default).

entries.title: Disable the Retail Demo service
entries.description: Sets the Retail Demo (RetailDemo) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: Retail Demo mode is only used on store display units; it is never needed on a personal machine.
sideEffects: Retail demo mode cannot be activated (it is a store-display feature).

entries.title: Disable the Payments and NFC/SE Manager service
entries.description: Sets the Payments and NFC/SE Manager (SEMgrSvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service manages NFC tap-to-pay and secure-element payments; on desktops and laptops without NFC hardware it never does anything.
sideEffects: NFC tap-to-pay and secure-element payment features stop working on devices that have NFC hardware.

entries.title: Disable the Recommended Troubleshooting service
entries.description: Sets the Recommended Troubleshooting (TroubleshootingSvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service runs the automatic ('recommended') troubleshooters that Microsoft pushes to the device; disabling it stops Windows from downloading and applying those automatically.
sideEffects: Windows no longer automatically downloads and applies recommended troubleshooters.

entries.title: Disable the Wallet service
entries.description: Sets the WalletService to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The Wallet feature is defunct on Windows 11; Microsoft lists the service as safe to disable.
sideEffects: The (defunct) Wallet feature is unavailable.

entries.title: Disable the WebClient (WebDAV) service
entries.description: Sets the WebClient (WebDAV) service to Disabled and stops it, removing the Windows WebDAV redirector.
entries.rationale: WebDAV was deprecated in November 2023 and the redirector is a known credential-leak vector (NTLM leak to remote WebDAV shares). Disabling it is a recommended hardening step for machines that do not open WebDAV or SharePoint UNC paths.
sideEffects: The \\server@SSL\ WebDAV UNC path form and SharePoint 'Open with Explorer' no longer work.

entries.title: Disable the Windows Insider service
entries.description: Sets the Windows Insider (wisvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service only supports the Windows Insider Program (preview-build flighting); it is unused on production machines.
sideEffects: Enrolling this device in the Windows Insider Program and receiving Insider preview flights no longer works until re-enabled.

entries.title: Disable Windows Media Player Network Sharing
entries.description: Sets the Windows Media Player Network Sharing (WMPNetworkSvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service only streams a Windows Media Player library to other DLNA devices; it is present only when Windows Media Player is installed and is unused on most machines.
sideEffects: Streaming a Windows Media Player library to other devices over the network (DLNA) stops working.

entries.title: Disable the Parental Controls service
entries.description: Sets the Parental Controls (WpcMonSvc) service to Disabled and stops it.
entries.rationale: The service backs Microsoft Family Safety monitoring; on machines with no child accounts it never does anything.
sideEffects: Microsoft Family Safety parental-control monitoring and enforcement stop working for child accounts on this PC.

entries.title: Disable the Windows AI Fabric service
entries.description: Sets the Windows AI Fabric (WSAIFabricSvc) service to Disabled and stops it. The service hosts the on-device AI models used by Copilot+ features.
entries.rationale: On Copilot+ PCs this service runs on-device inference for Recall, Click to Do and related AI features. Disabling it (Strict) removes that on-device AI processing; on hardware without Copilot+ the service is absent and this is a no-op.
sideEffects: Recall, Click to Do and other on-device Copilot+ AI features stop working.
Only present on Copilot+ PCs running 24H2 or later; a no-op elsewhere.

entries.title: Disable the Windows Mixed Reality services
entries.description: Sets the Windows Mixed Reality services (SharedRealitySvc, MixedRealityOpenXRSvc, spectrum, perceptionsimulation) and the VacSvc volumetric audio compositor to Disabled and stops them.
entries.rationale: Windows Mixed Reality was removed in Windows 11 24H2; on earlier builds these services only run with a WMR headset. Disabling them reclaims several background services on machines that never use WMR.
sideEffects: Windows Mixed Reality headsets and the OpenXR-via-WMR runtime stop working.
These services are removed in Windows 11 24H2, where the change is a harmless no-op.

entries.title: Disable the Peer Networking (PNRP) services
entries.description: Sets the Peer Name Resolution Protocol and peer-networking services (p2pimsvc, p2psvc, PNRPsvc, PNRPAutoReg) to Disabled and stops them.
entries.rationale: The PNRP peer-networking APIs were removed in Windows 11 24H2 and were only ever used by HomeGroup and a few legacy peer applications.
sideEffects: Legacy peer-to-peer applications and PNRP name resolution stop working.
PNRP is removed in Windows 11 24H2, where the change is a harmless no-op.

entries.title: Disable the sensor services
entries.description: Sets the sensor services (SensorService, SensorDataService, SensrSvc) to Disabled and stops them.
entries.rationale: On a desktop with no orientation, ambient-light or location sensors these services do nothing useful; disabling them is a Strict-tier option. On laptops, tablets and 2-in-1s they drive real features and this should not be applied there.
sideEffects: Automatic screen rotation, adaptive (ambient-light) brightness, sensor-based location and some Windows Hello sensor paths stop working.
Recommended only for desktops without sensors.

entries.title: Disable SSDP Discovery and UPnP Device Host
entries.description: Sets the SSDP Discovery (SSDPSRV) and UPnP Device Host (upnphost) services to Disabled and stops them.
entries.rationale: SSDP/UPnP discovery is used to find and cast to networked media devices; Microsoft lists it as safe to disable. It is a Strict-tier option because it removes device-casting discovery.
sideEffects: DLNA and cast-to-device discovery, some smart-TV and networked-printer discovery, and Xbox console streaming stop working.

entries.title: Disable the Xbox Live services
entries.description: Sets the Xbox Live services (XblAuthManager, XblGameSave, XboxNetApiSvc, XboxGipSvc) to Disabled and stops them.
entries.rationale: These services back Xbox app sign-in, cloud game saves, Xbox networking and controller/accessory management. Disabling them (Strict) suits users who do not use Xbox or Game Pass; gamers should keep them.
sideEffects: The Xbox app, Game Pass, cloud saves for Xbox Live titles and Xbox controller firmware / accessory management stop working.

entries.title: Disable the Messaging (SMS) user service
entries.description: Sets the per-user Messaging service (MessagingService) start type to Disabled via its service template key, so it does not start for any user after sign-in.
entries.rationale: The service only provides SMS text messaging through Phone Link; on machines that do not use Phone Link SMS it is unused. Because it is a per-user (template) service, this is written to the template key and takes effect at next sign-in.
sideEffects: SMS text messaging through Phone Link stops working.
Takes effect at next sign-in because it is a per-user service.

entries.title: Disable the Contact Data indexing user service
entries.description: Sets the per-user Contact Data service (PimIndexMaintenanceSvc) start type to Disabled via its service template key.
entries.rationale: The service indexes contact data for the People and Mail experiences, which are removed on current Windows 11; it is unused on those builds. As a per-user (template) service it is written to the template key and applies at next sign-in.
sideEffects: Contact indexing for People and Mail-style experiences stops.
Takes effect at next sign-in because it is a per-user service.

entries.title: Disable the User Data Storage and Access user services
entries.description: Sets the per-user User Data Storage (UnistoreSvc) and User Data Access (UserDataSvc) services to Disabled via their service template keys.
entries.rationale: These services store and broker Mail, People and Calendar data for the built-in apps that have been removed from current Windows 11; Microsoft lists them as safe to disable. As per-user (template) services they are written to the template keys and apply at next sign-in.
sideEffects: Apps that read Mail, People or Calendar data through these services lose access to it.
Takes effect at next sign-in because these are per-user services.
